[THOUGHT] The biopsy result—“papillary projections of epithelial-lined stroma with hyperplasia and atypia”—is highly characteristic of a phyllodes tumor. Phyllodes tumors are biphasic fibroepithelial neoplasms composed of both glandular (epithelial) and stromal components; the presence of papillary architecture, stromal hyperplasia, and cytologic atypia strongly supports this diagnosis. While benign phyllodes tumors exist, atypia raises concern for borderline or malignant potential—and rapid growth over three weeks is a classic clinical feature of phyllodes (especially compared to slow-growing fibroadenomas). Malignant breast carcinomas (e.g., ductal carcinoma) typically show invasive epithelial nests or ductal carcinoma in situ patterns—not papillary stromal projections with epithelial lining. This finding effectively rules out common carcinomas and inflammatory/infectious etiologies.

[DIAGNOSIS] Phyllodes tumor
